title: Why AUSL athlete Aleshia Ocasio Is raising awareness about cervical cancer prevention
summary: AUSL athlete Aleshia Ocasio shares how her grandmother's cervical cancer diagnosis shaped her approach to prevention, screening, and women's health.
body_markdown:
Long before becoming a professional softball player, Aleshia Ocasio understood the importance of preventive healthcare because of the story of her grandmother, Ines.


Ines died from[cervical cancer](https://womenshealth.labcorp.com/providers/cervical-cancer-screening/cervical-awareness-month) at just 39 years old. Although Aleshia never had the chance to meet her grandmother, Ines's legacy has remained an important part of her life.


"My family always told me about my grandma Ines, who she was, the kind of impact she had, and how she passed away," Aleshia says.


Growing up, Aleshia heard stories about her grandmother's life and the lasting influence she had on those who knew her. Family photos and memories kept her legacy alive, while also serving as a reminder of the importance of protecting Aleshia’s own health.


**A family history that sparked action**


Knowing her family's history helped shape the conversations Aleshia had about health from an early age. When she became eligible to receive the[HPV vaccine](https://womenshealth.labcorp.com/providers/cervical-cancer-screening) , her father made sure she was vaccinated.


"When I was old enough to get the HPV vaccine, my dad took me to the clinic to get my three rounds," Aleshia says.


That experience reinforced an important lesson: knowing your family's health history can help you make informed decisions about your own care. For Aleshia, taking preventive steps was a way to honor her grandmother's memory while reducing potential her own health risks in the future.


**Raising awareness about HPV screening**


Today, as a professional athlete in the Athletes Unlimited Softball League (AUSL), Aleshia is especially passionate about encouraging women to stay up to date with recommended cervical cancer screenings, even when they don’t have any symptoms.


"HPV screenings are way more accessible now," Aleshia says. "I encourage every woman to get routine checkups to make sure that they’re in tune with their body."


She hopes greater awareness about[screening and prevention](https://www.ondemand.labcorp.com/lab-tests/hpv-cervical-cancer-screening-test) will help more people take action early.


"Be able to identify something like this early and reduce your risk to help prevent cervical cancer," she says.


**A message for the next generation**


Even years after learning about her grandmother's story, Aleshia still becomes emotional when she thinks about the loved one she never had the chance to meet.


"I lost my grandmother way too soon," she says. "I wasn't able to meet her, and I see the impact that she's left on my family."


That loss continues to inspire her willingness to speak openly about prevention and awareness. "I hope this raises awareness," she says. "I hope that you get tested."


**The importance of prevention**


[Labcorp is working](https://www.labcorp.com/patients/ausl) with the AUSL to advance women’s health and support athlete well-being. As part of this collaboration, we're sharing stories from players about the role testing has played in their lives.&


Knowing her family’s health history played an important role in shaping how Aleshia approaches her health. We hope her story encourages you to learn about your health heritage so you can make more informed decisions and get the appropriate preventive care today.
